channel.title: DevFocus - 开发者聚焦
channel.description: 每日自动整理的开发者资讯：AI 热榜、GitHub 趋势、技术新闻

item.title: [hackernews] Margaret Hamilton has died
item.description: Margaret Hamilton has died. She is best known as a pioneer of software engineering, and this Hacker News submission points to the news, though the linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available. Anyone interested in the history of software and spaceflight should follow the original link.

item.title: [github_trending] morluto/rea
item.description: rea is a GitHub project that applies agents to reverse engineering, spanning app behaviour analysis all the way down to native binaries. Rather than being a single-purpose disassembler, it aims to let autonomous agents drive the investigation, which makes it relevant to security researchers and anyone who needs to understand closed-source software.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A Juejin post in which a developer describes spending roughly half a month in Codex after switching from Cursor. His takeaway is that Cursor still reads as an AI coding assistant, while Codex feels closer to a general-purpose agent that carries out tasks on its own. Useful for developers deciding which tool to adopt for daily work.

item.title: [zhihu] 日媒曝黑客黑掉软银旗下云平台后留下 225 封勒索信，结果运维找 7 小时没发现勒索信只是一味重启，如何看待？
item.description: Japanese media reported that attackers who breached a cloud platform under SoftBank left 225 ransom notes, yet the operations team spent seven hours without finding any of them and simply kept rebooting systems. The incident points to a detection and response gap rather than the intrusion itself. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available.

item.title: [36kr] 突发：OpenAI dots全面登陆手机，开口指挥Codex干活了
item.description: A 36Kr report says OpenAI's dots has rolled out fully on mobile, letting users issue spoken instructions to Codex. If accurate, it extends Codex from typed prompts to a voice-driven entry point, which matters for developers who want to delegate coding tasks away from a desktop. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available.

item.title: [infoq] Codex 和 Claude Code 都跑偏了，前 OpenAI 研究员称 Jev 出现前 AI 世界是个悲剧
item.description: Diogo Almeida, TypeSafe CEO and founder of Jev, told the Latent Space podcast that Codex and Claude Code belong to the same era in which AI merely assists humans. His answer is RLCD, reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions, which has models emit choices, scores and probabilities that code can consume directly, letting developers set thresholds on uncertainty for when to act and when to hand off.

item.title: [v2ex] [酷工作] 上海外企一年 contract 的职位： iOS/Android 开发，英语流利，月薪 60-70k，需要去现场办公
item.description: A foreign company in Shanghai is hiring iOS and Android developers on a one-year contract at 60-70k RMB per month, with fluent English required and on-site work. The Android role asks for 3+ years with the Android SDK and 5+ years in Java and other languages, while the iOS role wants 3+ years with the iOS SDK plus Swift and SwiftUI; bonuses include shipped Play Store apps, A/B testing and SQL.

item.description: A Juejin article argues the 2026 technical interview has changed: where two years ago candidates were asked to hand-write a Promise or explain React Fiber, interviewers now assume you work with AI and ask something else — if AI can write 80% of the code, why does the company still need you? Useful for developers preparing interviews and rethinking how they answer.

item.title: [infoq] OpenAI 高管亲述：我们是怎么在一周内做出 Jev 竞品的
item.description: InfoQ translated a Latent Space podcast interview with OpenAI's computer-use and API platform leads: each Dot agent gets its own cloud Linux machine and can drive browsers and desktop apps, while the Decisions API — started after seeing Jev — reached a working prototype in about a week by reusing Luna weights instead of retraining. The talk also covers how agents recover from errors and where humans should stay in the loop.

item.title: [infoq] @ 一下就能派活？谷歌推出办公 Agent，拥有独立账号、能够创建子 Agent，还能调用 Claude
item.description: At its Gemini at Work 2026 event on October 8, Google Cloud launched Gemini agent, an enterprise general-purpose AI agent introduced by CEO Thomas Kurian. It handles content creation, Q&A and code execution from a single prompt, can spin up sub-agents, and can be given its own email, calendar and persistent storage so it works as a long-term team member; it can also call Anthropic's Claude. Integration spans Workspace plus third-party tools like Slack, Jira and Salesforce.

item.title: [v2ex] [创业组队] 寻找技术合伙人｜一起做陪诊、陪护数字化平台 “PAPA”
item.description: A solo developer is looking for a technical co-founder for PAPA, a platform that digitizes hospital companion and eldercare services, after six months of market research. Target customers are the outsourcing firms that serve top-tier hospitals, though no contracts or revenue exist yet. A website, WeChat mini program and backend (React, Node.js, MySQL) are partly tested locally, with integration, permission isolation and deployment still to do; front- and back-end developers able to take over an

item.title: [infoq] 黄仁勋为微软站台：没有 Windows 就不会有英伟达，Satya 当场“讨市值”
item.description: At its October 8 Windows event, Microsoft introduced "hybrid intelligence": model routing and Windows ML let GitHub Copilot and other products switch between cloud and local models, and GitHub Copilot's HydraFusion will call local models running on Windows PCs directly. Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella traced the partnership from Windows 95, DirectX and CUDA to Azure's InfiniBand HPC, arguing agents are becoming a new kind of computer user. Microsoft shares rose roughly 0.1% that day.

item.title: [v2ex] [推广] 做了个小站：上传一张照片，生成 Jean Phil 风格的短视频
item.description: A developer built jeanphilai.org over a weekend: upload a frontal face photo, pick a scene, duration and suit color, and it returns a 9:16 vertical video in a few minutes, recreating the TikTok "Jean Phil" meme of a figure throwing air punches. Clips come out silent because the original music is copyrighted, and pricing is per second since the draft is cut to your chosen length. It is not free, given video-model costs.

item.title: [v2ex] [AI Tools 精品 AI 工具导航] 做了一个 Google Trends 上升词监控工具，适合 SEO 和选题研究
item.description: Trends Monitor is a small tool for querying Google Trends interest and rising related queries; you can save root keywords, turn on daily monitoring and review historical snapshots. Its author uses it as a lead-collection aid for SEO, content planning and product research, finding new terms first and then tracking how they move over time instead of judging from a single search.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 做了个 Mistral AI 工作空间，聊天、对话管理和成本估算都放到了一起
item.description: mistrallarge4.io is an AI workspace built around Mistral that puts chat, system-prompt and temperature settings, conversation history management and cost estimation in one place. It supports streaming output, Markdown and code blocks, JSON output, credit tracking and subscriptions, with history stored in the browser by default and optional cloud sync. The bilingual interface is mobile-friendly, and the author notes the independent project is not affiliated with Mistral AI.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 关于展示性网页+个人博客重构, 从 halo 和 wordpress 中摆脱出来, 意外发现很有意思的动静态结合的方法
item.description: The author migrated two sites off WordPress and Halo: WordPress was awkward to extend, while Halo's Java backend used too much memory and, after the 2.22.x upgrade, articles with purely numeric slugs started landing on the archive page. The replacement pairs a Go backend and dynamic admin UI with a Next.js build triggered on content changes, serving the generated static pages while keeping MCP, AI translation and SEO tasks dynamic.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] 把 Tripo Studio 连接到 Codex 的插件
item.description: Tripo Studio for Codex is an MIT-licensed open-source plugin, now at v0.3.4, that reuses your local Tripo Studio browser session and membership credits instead of requiring separately billed API keys. It wires the Studio pipeline into Codex through 68 MCP tools, covering High Detail models, Smart Mesh P2 meshes of 500–25,000 faces and Rig V3 auto-rigging, plus an embedded workspace for asset management and task queues.

Topics include round-trip tool calls that must always return a result, running the agent as a background process that fires system notifications when human input is needed, four-layer RAG memory, layered prompt assembly with progressive context compression, and a remote-machine plus fixed-container setup that spins up throwaway containers for sandboxed

item.title: [infoq] CLAUDE.md 还是 AGENTS.md？Anthropic 的答案是：以后都不用
item.description: The Claude Code team has confirmed it will support AGENTS.md, the instruction-file standard it previously refused to adopt, a stance that drew a public warning from Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke. On the Latent Space podcast, core team member Thariq Shihipar went further: as models get stronger, static instruction files like CLAUDE.md may eventually become unnecessary, so new projects can skip them until the same failure keeps recurring.

item.title: [infoq] 比 Astra 还贵！GPT-6.1 Sol 极速版上线，社区吐槽：“500 美元套餐都撑不过一天”
item.description: On October 8, OpenAI added an Ultrafast service tier to GPT-6.1 Sol, the model it shipped on September 29, in the Responses API; developers keep the same model name and just set the tier to ultrafast. Positioned as its fastest API tier, it is priced at six times the standard per-token rate and targets latency-sensitive workloads willing to pay more for speed.

item.title: [infoq] 当代码不再稀缺：大型工程 AI 狂欢下的确定性底座｜QCon上海
item.description: QCon Shanghai runs October 22-24, focused on engineering practice for the Harness AI era and covering AI-native architecture, agent runtime, AI infra, and agent safety and observability. Bilibili engineer Zhang Xinzheng will speak in the AI-driven software engineering track, drawing on backend, web and mobile work to argue that AI cuts code generation costs but not the cost of delivering correctness, and will cover constraints, localization, verification and measurement.

item.title: [infoq] Rails 之父 DHH 狂吹 Rust 快 150 倍，被开发者翻代码后群嘲
item.description: At Rails World 2026, DHH called Rust the ugliest programming language of the past 40 years, yet said he loves it as long as agents write the code and he never has to read it. He had agents rewrite 37signals' Campfire chat app in Elixir, Go and Rust; loading a chat room page, Rust hit 36,260 requests per second, roughly 150x Rails, 50x Elixir and 9.4x Go.

item.title: [infoq] OpenAI 只用 15 天，就杀死了估值 100 亿美元的 Jev？
item.description: At its DevDay, OpenAI introduced a Decisions API built on GPT-6 Luna, its smallest and cheapest model, which picks from preset options and returns a confidence score. OpenAI cites 150ms latency versus 1.6 seconds for calling Luna directly on the same task. It's in limited preview with pricing and option counts undisclosed, and closely mirrors the core capability of Jev, which launched just 15 days earlier — prompting a "Jev Is Dead" thread on Reddit.

item.title: [infoq] 金融监管领域的 Harness 实践：让知识与数据驱动 Agent 稳定运行
item.description: Yu Haojun, chief engineer at Zhongruan Rongxin, gave a talk at AICon 2026 Shenzhen on Harness practices in financial regulatory reporting. His approach combines knowledge and data foundations, a controlled state machine, and full-chain traceability to turn free-form agents into strictly governed systems that would rather abstain than answer wrong. The domain demands near-100% accuracy and zero tolerance for error, making it relevant to teams deploying agents in heavily regulated industries.

item.description: A Hacker News post about a small tool pitched as workplace self-defence against people who steal your time. It plays plausible fake meeting audio on demand: pick a meeting, press play, and look busy. It's aimed at remote or office workers who want a low-effort excuse to fend off constant interruptions.

item.title: [hackernews] Whistle: Speech to Text in 16.9 MB
item.description: Whistle is an open speech recognition model that ships in just 16.9 MB and runs on the same CPU engine as Needle. It transcribes seven languages and returns its first token in 11 ms, and since it can load alongside Needle, one binary can turn a clip straight into tool calls — useful for lightweight voice interfaces on local or edge hardware.

item.description: AnyPS5 converts PS5 executables into Linux and Windows native format via a relinker, plus implementations of system prx libraries suited to dynamic linking, with no emulation or separate runtime process. item.description: A long-form Juejin post lays out best practices for Codex, arguing that you should first understand how the model behaves before putting it to work. It walks through familiar failure modes: strong models producing unstable results, big swings when a task is rephrased, drift as conversations get longer, and more features than most people know how to use.

The question asks whether the buyer's conduct is illegal. The linked page isn't summarized here; it touches on abuse of refund-only policies and the cost of chasing small claims.

item.description: This Juejin post examines why ChatGPT-written novels tend to fall apart around chapter 30, citing symptoms such as a character's sister changing names and foreshadowing planted in chapter 5 never paying off. It treats the failure as an engineering problem and lays out solutions, making it useful for anyone attempting long-form serialized writing with an LLM.

item.description: The author notes that AI now lets one person finish three days of work in one, but managers know this too, so more proposals and tighter deadlines pour in and refill the saved time. The argument is that the real risk isn't being replaced, but producing a lot without accumulating reusable skills or assets. It speaks to developers who adopted AI tools and somehow feel more drained.

item.title: [github_trending] mattpocock/skills
item.description: Matt Pocock has published his personal agent skills, the set he uses daily for real engineering rather than vibe coding. They are deliberately small, composable, model-agnostic and meant to be forked and adapted, in contrast to process-owning approaches like GSD, BMAD and Spec-Kit that he says take control away from you. Aimed at developers who want a maintainable skill set for their coding agents.

item.title: [github_trending] cathrynlavery/diagram-design
item.description: cathrynlavery/diagram-design is an agent skill that renders diagrams as a single self-contained HTML + SVG file in your own brand, covering 44 diagram types and supporting Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Factory Droid and Pi. It deliberately drops shadows and avoids what the author calls Mermaid slop. Aimed at developers who need diagrams inside docs but find existing generators too templated.

item.title: [github_trending] anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins
item.description: Anthropic open-sourced 11 plugins for knowledge workers to use in Claude Cowork, each bundling the skills, connectors, slash commands and sub-agents for a specific job function, and they also work with Claude Code. The company says the out-of-the-box versions are only a starting point and the real value comes from customizing them with your own tools, terminology and processes.

item.title: [github_trending] hugohe3/ppt-master
item.description: hugohe3/ppt-master turns documents or topics into native PowerPoint decks with AI, using real shapes, transitions and animations, generating data-backed charts and tables on demand and audio narration from speaker notes. It is released under the MIT license. It fits people who need decks they can keep editing by hand instead of flattened image slides.

item.title: [github_trending] multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills
item.description: This GitHub repo, andrej-karpathy-skills, is a single CLAUDE.md file that modifies Claude Code's behavior based on Andrej Karpathy's observations of common LLM coding pitfalls. It targets issues like models running with wrong assumptions, overcomplicating code, and failing to clean up. Useful for developers who want to apply Karpathy's guidance directly to Claude Code.

item.title: [github_trending] mksglu/context-mode
item.description: Context Mode is an optimization layer for AI coding agents that sandboxes tool output, which it says cuts context usage by 98%, persists session memory, and enforces routing across 17 platforms via MCP plus hooks. It ships as an npm package under the ELv2 license, aimed at developers whose agents keep blowing through their context window.

item.title: [github_trending] flutter/flutter
item.description: flutter/flutter is Google's open source SDK for building mobile, web and desktop apps from one codebase, and it can be adopted alongside existing code. The repository holds the framework source and issue tracker, while install and usage docs live on flutter.dev. Relevant to anyone evaluating cross-platform stacks or planning to contribute patches.
